page: Amazon Web Services r6g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz without multithreading, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense deployments. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight solid memory bandwidth and consistent multi-core performance, achieving 126.06 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 57.75 GB/sec in large-block write tasks. In synthetic compute evaluations, the multi-core stress-ng score reaches 12132.45 and Geekbench multi-core registers at 5463.0, while Clang software compilation scores 8825.0. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects lower instructions-per-clock metrics, with Geekbench single-core scoring 961.0 and gzip compression displaying weak throughput. Dedicated encryption hardware tests and text parsing similarly show reduced relative performance compared to general-purpose x86 alternatives.

With no integrated GPUs and lower floating-point inference metrics, the instance is not suited for hardware-accelerated machine learning or dense neural network inference. The absence of local solid-state drives also requires planning for external storage latencies. However, the hardware profile delivers efficient memory scaling without overprovisioning compute resources, making it an effective choice for in-memory caches such as Redis, relational database systems, and intermediate data transformation services.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.2xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running on the Nitro system. It is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory to achieve an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external storage volumes, while network performance features a 2 Gbps baseline. Benchmarks indicate balanced multi-core and memory capabilities, reaching 126.06 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory reads and handling up to 9.91 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded execution, cryptographic throughput, and LLM token generation are comparatively weak, the high memory density provides cost-efficient operational headroom for in-memory caching layers, search engines, and relational databases.
